Thanks for the redline. We ran this past our legal team and attached DataCorp's annotated version — the majority are standard procurement asks. A few points of note:

Hi Sophie / Marissa,

Thanks — I reviewed DataCorp's annotated DPA and mapped it to Redwood's program. High-level positions below and proposed compromise language (attached).

1) EU transfers / SCCs: Redwood uses EU SCCs for transfers where required and is prepared to attach a standard SCC exhibit. We will not sign a regime that requires per-request assessment of transfer mechanisms; the SCC exhibit + documented safeguards should be sufficient. Proposed language: "Provider shall implement EU SCCs (or later-approved equivalent) for transfers of personal data from the EEA and shall maintain documented safeguards listed in Exhibit B."

2) Subprocessors: We are fine with a public subprocessor list and a 30-day notification mechanism for additions, with the ability to suspend a subprocessor only where DataCorp reasonably demonstrates material risk. Proposed: "Provider will publish its list of subprocessors on a public page and will provide 30 days' notice for additions; Customer may object only where material risk is demonstrated."

3) Audit clause: We prefer no on-site audits. We can offer an annual SOC 2 Type II report and a scoped remote audit under NDA. Proposed: "Customer may request one remote audit per 12 months; Provider will provide SOC 2 Type II reports and reasonable cooperation; on-site audits require prior written agreement and are subject to limited scope and scheduling constraints."

4) Liability cap: We can accept a cap tied to annual fees for the contractual year, but for pilot customers we prefer a defined multiple (e.g., 12 months' fees). We can be flexible in negotiations — propose to close at 12 months' fees.

5) Breach notification: Redwood commits to notification without unreasonable delay and to provide ongoing updates. We cannot guarantee investigatory timelines in the contract; we will commit to initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware for incidents affecting confidentiality or integrity.

I've attached a redline with these edits and short commentary. If DataCorp can align on SCC exhibit + public subprocessors + SOC 2 substitution for on-site audits, we can likely move to DocuSign within a few days.

Attachments:
- Redwood_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (updated with counsel notes)
- redline-summary.md

Happy to discuss live if helpful.

Best,
Laura Bennett
